title: Signal Sort
instruction: What does this action tell the recommender about the item?

items.text: Watched a video to the end
Bought the product after clicking it
items.why: A costly action: a very strong positive.

items.text: Saved it to a playlist or wishlist
items.why: Deliberate effort to come back later.
You attach your reputation to it.
You stated your intent in your own words.

items.text: Paused a video halfway and never came back
items.why: Boredom and a phone call look identical in the log.

items.text: Left a video playing in a background tab
items.why: A 'view' that may be background noise: nobody was necessarily watching.

items.text: Bought one children's toy among years of purchases for yourself
items.why: Probably a gift. A purchase is normally strong, but this one may say nothing about your taste.
An explicit, effortful rejection: the clearest 'no' there is.
In music, an early skip is a deliberate 'not this'. Skips are rarely accidental.

items.text: Opened an article and bounced back within 2 seconds
items.why: Short dwell is a classic implicit negative: the page didn't deliver what the headline promised.
A strong negative that a click log alone would miss.

debrief: Effortful actions are strong signals, and 'no' is information too: production systems often weight a rejection more than a missing click. Passive or out-of-character actions are ambiguous. Every one of them is a digital footprint.
